questions.prompt: At first light let us advance, lest the enemy see the legion.
questions.answer: Prīmā lūce prōgrediāmur nē hostis legiōnem videat.

questions.prompt: May the gods grant that the fearless hero return home.
questions.answer: Dī concēdant ut hērōs intrepidus domum redeat.

questions.prompt: Let him not conceal the truth, however grievous it may be.
questions.answer: Nē vēritātem dissimulet, quamvīs gravis sit.

questions.prompt: Let us rise before the sun, so that we may finish the journey.
questions.answer: Ante sōlem oriāmur, ut iter cōnficiāmus.

questions.prompt: The general sends scouts ahead so that they may explore the woods.
questions.answer: Dux explōrātōrēs praemittit ut silvās explōrent.

questions.prompt: We build a lofty rampart so that the pack-animals may be safe.
questions.answer: Altum vāllum exstruimus ut iūmenta tūta sint.

questions.prompt: She hides the sacred fillet lest the curious crowd behold it.
questions.answer: Vittam sacram cēlat nē cūriōsa turba cernat.

questions.prompt: I ask why the fearless soldiers do not fear death.
questions.answer: Rogō cūr mīlitēs intrepidī mortem nōn timeant.

questions.prompt: The commander wonders who is guarding the camp by night.
questions.answer: Imperātor mīrātur quis castra nocte custōdiat.

questions.prompt: It is uncertain when the dead hero may rise again.
questions.answer: Incertum est quandō hērōs mortuus resurgat.

questions.prompt: We do not know how great the strength of the legion may be.
questions.answer: Nescīmus quanta legiōnis vīs sit.

questions.prompt: Would that the fearless leader were present in the battle!
questions.answer: Utinam dux intrepidus in proeliō adsit!

questions.prompt: May eternal glory be granted to the fallen soldiers.
questions.answer: Utinam mīlitibus mortuīs glōria aeterna dētur.

questions.prompt: Would that the curious traveler perceive the danger!
questions.answer: Utinam viātor cūriōsus perīculum sentiat!

questions.prompt: May the gods look upon us and preserve the city.
questions.answer: Utinam dī nōs aspiciant et urbem servent.

questions.prompt: The orator speaks slowly so that the crowd may understand his words.
questions.answer: Ōrātor lentē loquitur ut turba verba eius intellegat.

questions.prompt: We close the gates lest the fierce enemy enter the city by night.
questions.answer: Portās claudimus nē hostis ferōx urbem nocte intret.

questions.prompt: The farmer works hard so that his children may not suffer hunger.
questions.answer: Agricola strēnuē labōrat nē līberī famem patiantur.

questions.prompt: The maiden hides the letter so that her stern mother may not read it.
questions.answer: Virgō epistulam cēlat nē māter sevēra eam legat.

questions.prompt: Let us sing songs while the sacred fire burns upon the altar.
questions.answer: Cantēmus carmina dum ignis sacer in altārī ārdet.

questions.prompt: Would that peace might endure throughout the whole world!
questions.answer: Utinam pāx per tōtum orbem permaneat!

questions.prompt: Let the brave young man dare great deeds, though danger threatens.
questions.answer: Audeat iuvenis fortis magna facta, quamquam perīculum imminet.

questions.prompt: May the gods be favorable to the sailors crossing the deep sea.
questions.answer: Sint deī nautīs altum mare trānseuntibus propitiī.

questions.prompt: The nurse asks why the infant weeps in the silent night.
questions.answer: Nūtrīx rogat cūr īnfāns nocte silentī fleat.

questions.prompt: I do not know where the wandering birds seek their nests.
questions.answer: Nesciō ubi volucrēs errantēs nīdōs petant.

questions.prompt: It is uncertain how great the strength of the enemy may be.
questions.answer: Incertum est quantae sint hostium vīrēs.

questions.prompt: The judge asks who possesses the plundered treasure.
questions.answer: Iūdex quaerit quis thēsaurō raptō potiātur.

questions.prompt: The general chooses soldiers to guard the bridge faithfully.
questions.answer: Dux mīlitēs legit quī pontem fidēliter custōdiant.

questions.prompt: Let us honor the gods, that they may protect our homeland.
questions.answer: Deōs colāmus, ut patriam nostram tueantur.

questions.prompt: The teacher explains the matter clearly so that the pupils may not err.
questions.answer: Magister rem clārē explicat nē discipulī errent.

questions.prompt: Send a messenger to announce the victory to the citizens.
questions.answer: Mitte nūntium quī cīvibus victōriam nūntiet.

questions.prompt: May the young man's noble character please the stern master.
questions.answer: Placeat indolēs generōsa iuvenis dominō sevērō.

questions.prompt: Let us strive with all our strength lest liberty perish.
questions.answer: Omnibus vīribus nītāmur nē lībertās pereat.

questions.prompt: Would that the eloquent advocate were present to defend the accused!
questions.answer: Utinam patrōnus disertus adsit ut reum dēfendat.

questions.prompt: The mother watches the fire lest a flame touch the sleeping infant.
questions.answer: Māter ignem observat nē flamma īnfantem dormientem tangat.

questions.prompt: Let us give thanks to the gods, since peace is present in the land.
questions.answer: Grātiās deīs agāmus, quod pāx in terrā adest.

questions.prompt: The teacher asks whether the boys understand the difficult poem.
questions.answer: Magister rogat num puerī carmen difficile intellegant.

questions.prompt: May we be brave when the hostile army approaches the walls.
questions.answer: Fortēs sīmus cum exercitus hostīlis mūrōs appropinquet.

questions.prompt: The frightened citizens flee so that the savage enemy may not capture them.
questions.answer: Cīvēs territī fugiunt nē hostis saevus eōs capiat.

questions.prompt: Let us honor the memory of those who died for their homeland.
questions.answer: Memoriam eōrum quī prō patriā periērunt colāmus.

questions.prompt: I do not know how great the danger may be in the deep forest.
questions.answer: Nesciō quantum perīculum in silvā altā sit.
